title: SSL/TLS Connection Encryption
description: Secure data in transit with TLS certificates, configure sslmode (verify-full), and mandate encrypted connections.

data.text: Unencrypted database traffic exposes plain-text SQL statements, query results, and passwords to network eavesdroppers. PostgreSQL supports native SSL/TLS encryption for all client-server communication.

rows: Encrypts traffic, but does not verify server identity against CA certificate.
Verifies server certificate against trusted Root CA.
Verifies certificate and matches host name against certificate CN/SAN. Industry standard!

data.text: Configuring the server certificate enables TLS, but the security comes from the client's `sslmode`. Only `verify-full` both encrypts the connection and verifies that the server certificate matches the hostname, which is what stops a man-in-the-middle attack. You can also restrict which hosts must use TLS in `pg_hba.conf`.

data.title: Require TLS in pg_hba.conf and verify from the client
data.content: `hostssl` matches only encrypted connections, so the first rule rejects anything that is not encrypted. `hostnossl` is never listed, so plaintext is impossible.
data.code:
# postgresql.conf
ssl = on
ssl_cert_file = '/etc/postgresql/server.crt'
ssl_key_file  = '/etc/postgresql/server.key'
ssl_min_protocol_version = 'TLSv1.2'

# pg_hba.conf: only allow encrypted remote connections
hostssl  all  all  0.0.0.0/0  scram-sha-256

# Client connection string
# postgresql://app@db.example.com:5432/app?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/etc/ssl/root.crt

data.title: verify-ca is not enough
data.text: `sslmode=require` encrypts but does not verify the certificate, so an attacker with a valid certificate for any domain can intercept the connection. `verify-ca` checks the certificate chain but not the hostname. Only `verify-full` checks both. In production connection strings, `sslmode=verify-full` with a pinned `sslrootcert` is the correct choice.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always use `sslmode=verify-full` in production connection strings to prevent MITM attacks.
Reject unencrypted connections in `pg_hba.conf` using `hostssl` instead of `host`.
